summary: Henri Cordier worked in sinology and history/archaeology. After studying at Lycée Chaptal, he served as a professor at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales (~1881–1925) and École Libre des Sciences Politiques/Sciences Po (~1886–1925).

Henri Gaidoz worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. Educated at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and under Albrecht Weber (1865), he held posts at the École Libre des Sciences Politiques (1872–1908) and École Pratique des Hautes Études (1876).

Henri Hubert studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and the École Normale Supérieure (~1892–1895). In religious studies and history/archaeology, he held appointments at the National Archaeological Museum (~1898–1927), École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1901–1927), and École du Louvre (~1904–1927).
Henri Lévy-Bruhl studied under Marcel Mauss. He held posts at Université de Lille Faculté de droit (1919–1929), Paris Law Faculty (~1930–1955), and École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Henri Maspero studied under Édouard Chavannes (1907) and at institutions including EFEO. Working in sinology, religious studies, and linguistics, he held chairs at the Collège de France (1918–1945), EPHE (~1928–1944), and Sorbonne/University of Paris (~1937–1944).

Henri Massé was an expert in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He held posts at the University of Algiers (~1916–1927) and École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (~1927–1958).

Henrik Samuel Nyberg worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and religious studies. After studying at Uppsala University in 1908, he taught at Fjellstedt School (~1916–1919) and served as lecturer and professor at Uppsala University (~1919–1956).
Henrik Zilliacus worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Helsinki (~1926–1936) and subsequently held a post there (~1944–1974).

Henry Beveridge was active in Indology and history/archaeology after studying at the University of Glasgow (~1853–1856) and Queen's University Belfast (1856). He served in the Indian Civil Service (1857–1893) and as President of The Asiatic Society (1890–1891).

Henry Clarke Warren specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard University (~1875–1879), Johns Hopkins University (1879), and the University of Oxford, studying under Charles Rockwell Lanman (1879), Maurice Bloomfield (~1881–1884), and T. W. Rhys Davids.

Henry Creswicke Rawlinson worked in history/archaeology and Iranian/Central Asian studies after attending Great Ealing School and Middlesex University. He served in the East India Company (~1827–1858), Foreign Office (~1859–1860), and Royal Asiatic Society (Director 1862; President 1878–1881).

Henry George Keene was active in Iranian/Central Asian studies and Indology. He studied at Fort William College (~1801–1804) and Sidney Sussex College (1811–1815), served in the East India Company (~1800–1811), and became professor at East India Company College (1824–1834).

Henry Hamilton Hadley studied at Yale College (~1843–1845), Union Theological Seminary (~1847–1848), and Andover (~1848–1853). In religious studies and linguistics, he held posts at Union Theological Seminary (1858, 1862) and Yale Divinity School (1861).

Henry Herbert Dodwell worked in history/archaeology and Indology. After studying at Lord Williams's School and St John's College, Oxford (~1898–1902), he served in the Indian Educational Service (1908–1922) and as professor at SOAS University of London (1922–1946).

Henry Hoenigswald specialized in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the universities of Munich (1932–1933), Zurich (1933–1934), Padua (1934–1936), and Florence (~1936–1937), later holding a post at the University of Pennsylvania (~1948–1985).
Henry Martyn was active in linguistics and religious studies. He studied at Truro Cathedral School, St John's College (~1797–1801), and under John Borthwick Gilchrist (~1804–1805).
Henry Miers Elliot was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Winchester College (~1820–1826) and subsequently worked as a civil servant for the East India Company (~1826–1853).

Henry Pitts Forster was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served in the East India Company and Bengal Civil Service (~1783–1815), and was Master of the Calcutta Mint at the India Government Mint, Kolkata (1803–1804).

Henry Shiu works in Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Toronto (-2006) and studied under Shek-Wing Tam (1993), Leonard C. D. C. Priestley, David B. Waterhouse, and Willard Gurdon Oxtoby (1998).

Henry Sullivan Jarrett was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Secretary and Member of the Board of Examiners in Calcutta (~1870–1892), where he succeeded Heinrich Blochmann.
